name: Steel mills and ferrous scrap (Nucor, Steel Dynamics, Cleveland-Cliffs, U.S. Steel)
description: Steel for ductile-iron and steel pipe, steel poles, truck bodies and valve bodies. Ductile-iron pipe makers melt mostly ferrous scrap. Only the utility-materials slice is shown.

name: Pipe resin producers (PE: Chevron Phillips, Dow, ExxonMobil, LyondellBasell; PVC: Westlake, Shintech, OxyVinyls)
description: Polyethylene resin for gas mains and services (plastic is ~58% of US gas distribution main) and PVC for water and sewer pipe.

name: Copper and aluminum rod and redraw (Freeport-McMoRan, Southwire rod mills, Alcoa, Century Aluminum)
description: Copper and EC-grade aluminum for overhead conductor and underground distribution (URD) cable. Metal is roughly 60-70% of cable value.

name: Truck chassis makers (Daimler Truck/Freightliner, PACCAR, International)
description: Class 6-8 chassis that aerial-device, digger-derrick, sewer-cleaner and hydrovac bodies are mounted on.

name: Craft training pipeline (IBEW-NECA JATCs, LIUNA and UA programs, lineworker schools, community colleges)
description: Apprenticeships and pre-apprentice schools that supply lineworkers, gas fitters and pipe layers. Quanta owns Northwest Lineman College (acquired 2017 per company history; not re-verified), an example of a contractor buying its own labor pipeline. Lineworker supply, not demand, is the binding constraint in storm seasons.

name: Imperial Group (Imperial Recycling, Exeon, Midwest Industrial Metals; affiliate Mayco Industries)
description: Fulton's family metals group (founded 1962, Chicago). Recovers copper and aluminum from insulated and armored cable and granulates wire into clean chops. Mayco Industries (lead sheet and shot) could absorb lead service-line scrap. Ferrous cast-iron scrap is outside Imperial's non-ferrous core and would be brokered.

name: Stainless Foundry & Engineering (SFE)
description: Milwaukee stainless and high-alloy sand and investment castings (to ~200 lb) for energy, nuclear and power-generation OEMs; ~6-week lead times. Fits specialty valve bodies and outage replacement parts, not commodity ductile-iron valves.

name: Panther Metalflow
description: Swiss-type CNC turning and zinc cast-in-place assemblies (Walled Lake MI); ISO 9001, ITAR. Could turn brass and steel fittings, meter-set and service-valve parts.

name: AFCO Industries
description: Aluminum, composite and vinyl building products plus CNC fabrication and contract manufacturing (LA, MS, AL, IL). Candidate supplier of aluminum compartments, toolboxes and platforms for utility truck bodies.
ownership: Fulton Asset Management and Ashland Capital (closed Jul 31, 2025)

name: Transend Logistics
description: Chicago 3PL and freight broker: flatbed, dry van, drayage, cross-dock and cross-border lanes. No heavy-haul capability, which fits pipe and fittings freight.

name: United Rentals
description: Largest US equipment rental firm. Its Specialty segment (Trench Safety, Power and HVAC, Fluid Solutions) supplies trench shoring, pumps, generators and compact equipment to gas, water and line contractors.
size_label: Total revenue ~$16B (2025, approx.); utility-contractor slice est. $0.45-0.95B

name: Sunbelt Rentals
description: Second-largest US rental firm; trench safety, power and climate and general equipment for utility contractors.

name: Custom Truck One Source
description: Specialty rental and sales of utility trucks (aerial devices, digger derricks, cranes) to T&D contractors and utility fleets; formerly NESCO.

name: Altec
description: Dominant US maker of aerial devices and digger derricks for utilities and line contractors (Birmingham AL); also services and rents fleets.

name: Vermeer
description: Horizontal directional drills (HDD) and vacuum excavators used to bore services and underground distribution cable.

name: Ditch Witch (The Toro Company)
description: Compact HDD, trenchers and vacuum excavators; Toro bought Charles Machine Works (Ditch Witch) in 2019.

name: Federal Signal (Vactor, TRUVAC, Jetstream)
description: Sewer cleaners, hydro-excavation trucks and water-jetters sold to municipalities and contractors.

name: Mueller Water Products
description: Water valves, hydrants, brass service products and Echologics leak detection; sells mainly through waterworks distributors. Runs its own iron and brass foundries.

name: Badger Meter
description: Water meters, AMI and BEACON software sold mostly to municipal water utilities; meter swaps retire brass meters.

name: Itron
description: Electric, gas and water meters and AMI networks bought directly by utilities (utility-furnished, not via contractors).
size_label: Revenue ~$2.4B (2024, approx.); US utility slice est. $1.0-1.7B

name: Utility pipe makers (JM Eagle, WL Plastics, Westlake Pipe & Fittings, Diamond Plastics, McWane, U.S. Pipe, American Cast Iron Pipe)
description: PE gas pipe, PVC and ductile-iron water and sewer pipe. Most moves through distributors; utilities often furnish the pipe their contractors install.

name: Gas fittings, valves and regulators (GF Central Plastics, Kerotest, Dresser Utility Solutions, Mueller gas products, Honeywell/Elster)
description: Electrofusion and mechanical fittings, service and curb valves, regulators and meter-set parts for gas mains and services. Bodies are mostly ductile iron, steel, brass or PE; stainless is a niche.

name: Power cable and conductor makers (Southwire, Prysmian incl. General Cable and Encore Wire, Okonite, Nexans)
description: Overhead conductor and URD/feeder cable for reconductoring, undergrounding and cable-replacement programs.

name: Poles and line hardware (Stella-Jones, Koppers, Valmont, Hubbell Utility Solutions, MacLean Power Systems, Preformed Line Products)
description: Wood and steel poles, crossarms, insulators and connectors. 130-160M wood poles are in service; maintained poles last 70-80+ years versus ~35-year book life.

name: Insurance and surety (Liberty Mutual, Travelers, Chubb, Zurich; brokers Marsh, Aon, WTW)
description: Auto, general liability, workers' comp and wildfire exposure for field contractors; a fast-rising cost (Davey took a $34.5M insurance charge in FY2025). Typically 2-4% of contractor revenue (assumption).

name: Field craft labor (IBEW outside line, LIUNA, UA, IUOE and open-shop crews)
description: Wages and benefits of lineworkers, gas crews, pipe layers and operators; 45-55% of contractor revenue. NAICS 237130 alone employs 292,604 people at an average $90,207 (CBP 2023 via aggregator). Crews and qualifications rarely transfer between gas, electric and water.

name: Badger Infrastructure Solutions
description: Largest hydrovac (non-destructive excavation) provider; builds its own trucks. Works for utilities directly and as a subcontractor to contractors. FY2025 revenue $831.7M, adj. EBITDA 23.8%, revenue per truck per month $41,672.

name: Restoration, paving and traffic-control subs (e.g., AWP Safety, Flagger Force, local paving firms)
description: Street restoration, paving and flagging after main and service replacement; a large share of urban replacement cost (assumption: 10-25%).

name: Core & Main
description: Largest US waterworks distributor: pipe, valves, hydrants, fittings and meters to municipalities and contractors.

name: Ferguson (Waterworks)
description: Waterworks is one of Ferguson's customer groups; supplies water and sewer contractors and utilities.

name: MRC Global
description: Pipe, valves and fittings distributor with a large gas-utility business (PE pipe, fittings, meters under MRO supply contracts). Merger with DNOW announced Jun 2025 (status not re-verified).

name: Wesco (Utility & Broadband Solutions)
description: Utility MRO materials (cable, connectors, line hardware, poles) and storm-stock programs for IOUs and co-ops. UBS segment $5.5B (2025) incl. broadband.

name: Quanta Services
description: The original 1990s utility-services roll-up and the category leader: electric T&D, underground utility (gas distribution, pipeline integrity) and renewables. Even at this scale adj. EBITDA is ~10.1%; scale bought labor depth, MSA share and backlog ($43.98B), not premium margins.
size_label: FY2025 revenue $28.48B; in-scope MRO flows est. $7.2-12.0B

name: MasTec
description: Diversified infrastructure contractor. Power Delivery $4,176M at 8.1% segment EBITDA; Pipeline $2,138M at 14.9% (down from 18.3%). Absorbed the IEA renewables roll-up in 2022 (~$1.1B EV).
size_label: FY2025 revenue $14.3B, adj. EBITDA 8.0%; in-scope est. $1.7-2.9B

name: Primoris Services
description: Utilities segment (power delivery, gas operations, communications) ~$2.69B at 11.5% gross margin; the Energy segment is EPC construction.
size_label: FY2025 revenue ~$7.7B, adj. EBITDA ~6.9%; in-scope est. $1.7-2.5B

name: MYR Group
description: T&D segment $2.00B at a 7.4% operating margin; gross margin swung 8.6% to 11.6% on project write-downs, showing fixed-price risk.

name: Michels Corporation
description: Family-owned diversified contractor (Brownsville WI): gas distribution, power lines and trenchless water rehab. ENR Top 400 #38 and #9 power contractor; revenue undisclosed. Water work folded into the regional water flows.

name: Centuri Holdings
description: Closest public analogue to the thesis: gas and electric utility MSA replacement work, spun out of Southwest Gas (separation completed 2025). Base gross margin only 8.0%; adj. EBITDA 8.3%; net leverage cut to 2.5x.

name: Artera Services (Miller Pipeline, Minnesota Limited, Feeney)
description: Gas-first MRO roll-up: bought CenterPoint's Miller Pipeline and Minnesota Limited for $850M (2020). Moody's cut to Caa1 (2022) and S&P to CCC+ negative (Dec 2025): the most direct warning for a leveraged gas MRO platform. Also does water rehab and pipeline integrity (integrity not shown).

name: Energy Services of America
description: Small public gas and water distribution contractor in Appalachia: a scale reference for a FAM platform. Adj. EBITDA fell to 4.2% in FY2025.

name: Pike Corporation
description: T&D maintenance, storm restoration and engineering, ~12,000 employees, 400+ customers. TPG Rise Climate and La Caisse bought a majority from Lindsay Goldberg in Dec 2025 at a reported >$5B (unconfirmed). Revenue was ~$1.7B in 2020.

name: Asplundh Tree Expert
description: Largest utility vegetation-management and line-clearance firm; also line construction. Revenue ~$6.3B per Forbes (weak; other sources $4.5-4.7B), incl. non-US and non-utility work.

name: Davey Tree Expert
description: Employee-owned; utility vegetation management is its largest segment. FY2025 operating margin ~3.7% (5.5% ex a $34.5M insurance charge): recurring revenue, thin margins.

name: Osmose Utilities Services
description: Pole inspection, treatment and restoration (incl. co-ops); the 10-year inspect-and-treat cycle is what stretches pole life to 70-80+ years. Second sponsor (EQT, 2019).

name: USIC
description: Largest North American 811 locating and damage-prevention firm; bought Heath Consultants' gas-locating unit in 2025. The one proven cross-utility service, but a single service line. Only gas-utility locating is drawn; electric, water and telecom locates excluded.
size_label: Revenue not disclosed; gas locating est. $0.4-0.8B

name: Shermco Industries
description: NETA-accredited electrical testing roll-up: ~40 service centers, 600+ NETA technicians, built by buying regional NETA firms. Sold to Blackstone for ~$1.6B (Oct 2025); growth leaned on data centers and C&I.
size_label: Revenue not disclosed; est. $0.3-0.55B (from deal value, assumption)

name: Mistras Group
description: NDE and inspection consolidator; mostly oil and gas, with growing power generation. Stable but not growing; 12.6% adj. EBITDA.

name: Day & Zimmermann
description: ENR's #1 power O&M contractor for six straight years: nuclear and fossil outage maintenance and modifications. Outage work needs NRC Appendix B quality programs, a high entry barrier.

name: Team Inc
description: Inspection, heat treating and mechanical services, mostly refining and petrochemical; power is a minority. Net loss in FY2025 after a 2025 refinancing.

name: OEM field services (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Westinghouse, Framatome, Vestas)
description: Long-term service agreements and outage services by equipment makers. They capture the largest share of plant maintenance and sit outside the addressable pool for an independent roll-up.

name: Independent plant maintenance contractors (EnergySolutions incl. ex-Williams, BrandSafway, Babcock & Wilcox services, regional outage firms)
description: Non-OEM outage, boiler, balance-of-plant and renewable O&M work. Williams Industrial Services (nuclear and fossil maintenance plus water) went through Chapter 11 in 2023 and sold to EnergySolutions for $60M.

name: Azuria Water Solutions (Insituform) + Inframark
description: Ex-Aegion, taken private by New Mountain in 2021 ($963M announced) and refocused on water; CIPP sewer and water rehab plus Inframark contract O&M. Combination announced Jul 2025 at ~$2.5B combined revenue.
size_label: ~$2.5B combined revenue; US municipal flows est. $1.3-1.9B

name: Vortex Companies
description: Trenchless water and sewer rehab roll-up (~12 acquisitions); bought Tri-State Utilities and Pipe Vision from National Underground Group.

name: National Underground Group
description: ORIX-backed sewer inspection, cleaning and trenchless rehab platform.

name: USG Water Solutions (Utility Service Co)
description: Long-term water-tank maintenance contracts with municipalities; sold to Suez/United Water for $220M in 2008 (current owner not re-verified; likely Veolia after its Suez merger).

name: Regional gas and pipeline contractors (long tail)
description: Thousands of small and mid-size gas main, service and integrity contractors inside NAICS 237120/237110; part of ~18,877 utility-system construction firms (2017 Economic Census via NUCA). The pool FAM would buy from.

name: Regional line, vegetation and NETA testing firms (long tail)
description: Regional line contractors, tree crews and NETA-accredited testing firms (NAICS 237130: 7,112 establishments; includes telecom). Shermco's add-on pool.

name: Regional water and sewer contractors (long tail)
description: Main replacement, lead service-line, CIPP and valve/hydrant crews (NAICS 237110: ~10,600 firms). Most fragmented unit; buyers are municipal.

name: Atmos Energy
description: Largest gas-only US distributor (8 states). Spends most of its capex (~$3.6B in FY2025, approx.; not re-verified) on safety and reliability replacement, recovered through rate riders.

name: Southwest Gas
description: AZ, NV and CA gas utility and Centuri's former parent; still a major Centuri customer.

name: CenterPoint Energy (gas utilities)
description: Sold Miller Pipeline and Minnesota Limited (its in-house contractors) to PowerTeam/Artera in 2020 for $850M; continued work with them is likely but not verified.

name: Other gas LDCs (NiSource, Southern Company Gas, Spire, ONE Gas, National Grid, Con Edison, PSEG and others)
description: 1,367,851 miles of main (2023). Cast and wrought iron is ~1% of mains but 8% of main incidents; 16,337 miles left (2023), concentrated in NJ, NY, MA, PA and MI. Gas utilities invest ~$33-37B a year in safety.

name: PG&E
description: Electric and gas IOU. Its 1921 Caribou-Palermo line (~97 years old) started the 2018 Camp Fire; now spends heavily on vegetation management, undergrounding and hardening.

name: Duke Energy
description: Large Southeast IOU; historically Pike's largest customer (per past Pike filings; not re-verified).

name: Other electric IOUs (AEP, Southern, Dominion, Xcel, Exelon, FirstEnergy, Entergy and others)
description: EEI members plan ~$208B of capex in 2025 and >$1.1T over 2025-29; distribution capex $50.9B (2023), transmission $32.6B (2024). Only replacement, hardening and outsourced O&M is in scope.

name: Public power and co-ops (~2,000 municipal utilities, ~900 co-ops, TVA)
description: Serve ~28% of US retail kWh; buy line maintenance, vegetation and pole inspection, often from regional firms.

name: Constellation Energy
description: Largest US nuclear fleet; restarting Crane (ex-TMI-1, target 2027) under a Microsoft PPA and signed a Clinton PPA with Meta (per company announcements; not re-verified). Life extension locks in decades of refueling outages.

name: Other nuclear operators (Duke, Southern Nuclear, TVA, Vistra, Dominion, PSEG, Entergy, NextEra, Talen, Holtec)
description: NRC renewed 18 licenses (~17 GW) in 15 months; 80-year licenses now routine (Turkey Point, Surry, Browns Ferry, St. Lucie, Hatch). Regulated units' revenue sits in the tariff edges, so only merchant output is drawn to markets.

name: Gas and coal plant owners (IOUs and IPPs: Vistra, NRG and others)
description: Gas turbines run harder as load grows; the coal fleet averages 45 years and retires at ~50, so coal is a shrinking maintenance market.

name: Wind, solar and storage owners (NextEra Energy Resources, AES, Invenergy, Brookfield and others)
description: 53 GW added in 2025 and 86 GW planned for 2026; O&M pool est. $7-10B, largely captured by OEM service agreements and owners' in-house teams.

name: American Water Works
description: Largest US investor-owned water and wastewater utility; most capex goes to main replacement, recovered through PUC rates.

name: Municipal water and wastewater utilities (~50,000 community water systems, ~16,000 treatment works)
description: 33% of mains are >50 years old; 11.1 breaks per 100 miles a year; replacement pace implies a ~125-year cycle. EPA's 20-year need is $625B ($420.8B distribution); ~4.0M lead service lines (2025 update). Most O&M is in-house.

name: Gas transmission pipeline operators (Kinder Morgan, Williams, Energy Transfer, TC Energy)
description: Integrity digs, in-line inspection follow-up and maintenance; adjacent to, not inside, the thesis TAM.
size_label: Integrity and maintenance services in est. $1.4-3.0B

name: Data-center and C&I electrical owners
description: Owners of behind-the-meter substations and switchgear that buy NETA acceptance and maintenance testing; Shermco's fastest-growing customers. Outside the thesis TAM.

name: PUC-regulated electric tariffs (IOU rate base)
description: Capitalized replacement earns a regulated return in rate base; O&M does not. That is why replacement work under MSAs is the sturdier pool.

name: PUC-regulated gas tariffs (incl. infrastructure-replacement riders)
description: Replacement programs are recovered through riders and surcharges outside full rate cases. The federal leak-detection rule is not in force (withdrawn Jan 2025; new proposal sent to DOT Apr 2026).

name: Public power and co-op rates (local boards)
description: Rates set by city councils, utility boards and co-op members.

name: Water and sewer rates and municipal revenue bonds
description: Public water and wastewater spending was $113B in 2017 ($31B capital, $82B O&M); capital is largely bond-financed and repaid from rates.

name: Federal water programs (Clean Water and Drinking Water SRFs, IIJA supplemental, WIFIA)
description: FY2026 is the last year of IIJA supplemental SRF money ($2,603M each fund). Regular FY2026 funding is flat but earmarks leave net grants of ~$746M (CWSRF) and ~$411M (DWSRF): a federal cliff in FY2027.
size_label: FY2026 financing est. $10-18B incl. state match and revolving loans

name: Wholesale power markets and PPAs (ISO/RTO, bilateral)
description: Merchant generators sell energy and capacity here; PJM wholesale prices +~41% in 2026 (EIA STEO). Utilities' purchases for default service are embedded in the tariff edges, so this node is not additive with them.

name: Large-load tariffs and customer contributions (data centers)
description: Data-center electricity bills and contributions in aid of construction for interconnections; growth is concentrated in ERCOT and PJM and pays mostly for new construction, not maintenance.

name: Households (residential ratepayers)
description: Residential electricity revenue was $244.4B in 2024; residential use per customer fell 2.3% from 2009 to 2019 on efficiency. US population growth slowed to 0.5% in 2025, so households are not the growth driver.
size_label: Electricity $244.4B (2024) plus gas and water bills

name: Businesses and industry (commercial and industrial ratepayers)
description: Commercial ($185.0B) and industrial ($84.1B) electricity revenue in 2024, plus gas and water bills. Commercial sales lead 2026 growth at +3.8% (incl. data centers).
size_label: Electricity $269B (2024) plus gas and water bills

name: Data centers and hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta)
description: Data centers used 176 TWh in 2023 (4.4% of US use), heading to 325-580 TWh by 2028 (LBNL). Nuclear PPAs include Constellation-Microsoft (Crane), Constellation-Meta (Clinton) and Talen-Amazon (Susquehanna) (per company announcements; not re-verified).

name: Federal and state taxpayers
description: Fund SRF capitalization grants (federal) and the 20% state match; only ~4% of public water spending was federal in 2017.
